| `rentExempt` | `function rentExempt(space: u64): u64` | Rent-exempt minimum balance for an account of `space` bytes. |
| `TOKEN_ACCOUNT_SIZE` | `const TOKEN_ACCOUNT_SIZE: u64` | SPL Token's token account size, 165 bytes, for systemProgram.createAccount. |
| `MINT_SIZE` | `const MINT_SIZE: u64` | SPL Token's mint size, 82 bytes. |

## Token-2022 extension reads

Explained in [Calling other programs: Token-2022 extension reads](language-cpi.md#token-2022-extension-reads).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `transferFee` | `function transferFee(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount, amount: u64): u64` | The fee withheld when `amount` is sent now: the mint's Token-2022 TransferFeeConfig for the current epoch, 0 without it. |
| `transferFeeInverse` | `function transferFeeInverse(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount, amountReceived: u64): u64` | The fee withheld when the recipient is to get `amountReceived` (spl-token-2022's `calculate_inverse_epoch_fee`): send `amountReceived + transferFeeInverse(mint, amountReceived)`. 0 without TransferFeeConfig; fails (5100) where spl-token-2022 has no answer. |
| `transferFeeBasisPoints` | `function transferFeeBasisPoints(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): u16` | The TransferFeeConfig in force this epoch: its basis points (0 without the extension). |
| `transferFeeMaximum` | `function transferFeeMaximum(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): u64` | The TransferFeeConfig in force this epoch: its maximum fee (0 without the extension). |
| `extensionsWithin` | `function extensionsWithin(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount, types: u16[]): boolean` | Whether every Token-2022 extension of `account` is one of `types` (a list of u16 extension types, e.g. `[1n, 18n, 19n, 10n, 25n]`): a pool that accepts only mints it knows how to handle. |
| `hasExtension` | `function hasExtension(account: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount, extensionType: u16): boolean` | Whether a Token-2022 mint or token account carries extension `extensionType` (e.g. 9 NonTransferable, 7 ImmutableOwner). |
| `transferHookProgram` | `function transferHookProgram(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): Option<Pubkey>` | The TransferHook extension's program, if any. |
| `transferHookAuthority` | `function transferHookAuthority(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): Option<Pubkey>` | The TransferHook extension's authority (who may change the hook program), if any. |
| `permanentDelegate` | `function permanentDelegate(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): Option<Pubkey>` | The PermanentDelegate extension's delegate, if any (it can move or burn anyone's tokens). |
| `mintCloseAuthority` | `function mintCloseAuthority(mint: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): Option<Pubkey>` | The MintCloseAuthority extension's authority, if any. |
| `isTransferring` | `function isTransferring(tokenAccount: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): boolean` | Whether Token-2022 is transferring from this token account right now (its TransferHookAccount `transferring` flag): true inside a transfer hook called by Token-2022, false when the hook is invoked directly. |

## Transfer hooks

Explained in [Calling other programs: Implementing another program's interface (transfer hooks)](language-cpi.md#implementing-another-programs-interface-transfer-hooks).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `initExtraAccountMetas` | `function initExtraAccountMetas(payer: Mut<Signer>, account: AccountMeta, mint: AccountMeta, systemProgram: SystemProgram, extraAccounts?: ExtraAccountMeta[]): void` | Create the transfer-hook validation account (an ExtraAccountMetaList) at PDA ["extra-account-metas", mint], listing the extra accounts Token-2022 passes to the hook after the standard four and this account (so the first extra account has index 5). |
| `updateExtraAccountMetas` | `function updateExtraAccountMetas(payer: Mut<Signer>, account: AccountMeta, mint: AccountMeta, systemProgram: SystemProgram, extraAccounts?: ExtraAccountMeta[]): void` | Rewrite this program's existing ExtraAccountMetaList for `mint` (Rust `ExtraAccountMetaList::update`), resizing it to the new list; `payer` tops it up to the rent of the new size when needed. |
| `ExtraAccountMeta` | `type ExtraAccountMeta` | One extra account of a transfer hook's ExtraAccountMetaList: a fixed address, or a PDA from seeds (see initExtraAccountMetas). |
| `ExtraAccountSeed` | `interface ExtraAccountSeed` | A seed of an extra account resolved by Token-2022 at transfer time (seedAccountKey, seedAccountData, seedInstructionData). |
| `seedAccountKey` | `function seedAccountKey(index: bigint): ExtraAccountSeed` | Seed::AccountKey: the key of the account at this index of the execute instruction. |
| `seedAccountData` | `function seedAccountData(index: bigint, offset: bigint, length: bigint): ExtraAccountSeed` | Seed::AccountData: `length` bytes at `offset` of the data of the account at `index`. |
| `seedInstructionData` | `function seedInstructionData(offset: bigint, length: bigint): ExtraAccountSeed` | Seed::InstructionData: `length` bytes at `offset` of the execute instruction's data. |

## Metaplex Core

Explained in [Calling other programs: Metaplex Core](language-cpi.md#metaplex-core).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MplCoreProgram` | `interface MplCoreProgram` | Metaplex Core (CoREEN…), address checked. |
| `CorePlugin` | `type CorePlugin` | A Metaplex Core plugin, written as an object literal (Core's Plugin enum, with its authority when it is added). |
| `CorePluginKind` | `type CorePluginKind = CorePlugin["kind"] \| "Groups"` | The name of a Metaplex Core plugin, as `removePlugin` and the plugin readers take it. |
| `CorePluginAuthority` | `type CorePluginAuthority = "none" \| "owner" \| "updateAuthority" \| Pubkey` | Who manages a Metaplex Core plugin: `"owner"`, `"updateAuthority"`, `"none"` (nobody: fixed), or an address. |
| `CoreExternalPlugin` | `type CoreExternalPlugin` | A Metaplex Core external plugin adapter, written as an object literal: data a third party writes (`AppData`), an account that approves or rejects lifecycle events (`Oracle`), or a program called on them (`LifecycleHook`); the `Linked` forms go on a collection, for each of its assets. |
| `CoreExternalPluginKey` | `type CoreExternalPluginKey` | Which external plugin: an AppData by its data authority, an Oracle by its base address, a LifecycleHook by its program. |
| `CoreLifecycleCheck` | `interface CoreLifecycleCheck` | When a Core lifecycle event reaches an external plugin, and what the plugin may do about it. |
| `CoreExtraAccount` | `type CoreExtraAccount` | An account Core passes to an external plugin: one it already has, or an address. |
| `coreAssetOwner` | `function coreAssetOwner(asset: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): Pubkey` | The owner of a Metaplex Core asset (owner program and account type checked). |
| `coreAssetCollection` | `function coreAssetCollection(asset: AccountMeta \| RemainingAccount): Option<Pubkey>` | The collection a Metaplex Core asset belongs to, if any. |

## Compressed NFTs

Explained in [Calling other programs: Compressed NFTs (Bubblegum)](language-cpi.md#compressed-nfts-bubblegum).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BubblegumProgram` | `interface BubblegumProgram` | Metaplex Bubblegum (BGUMAp…), compressed NFTs on SPL Account Compression. |
| `CompressedLeaf` | `interface CompressedLeaf` | The leaf a transfer or burn replaces, as an indexer (DAS getAssetProof / getAsset) reports it. |
| `CompressedLeafRef` | `interface CompressedLeafRef` | A leaf whose data and creator hashes the instruction computes from the metadata passed with it. |
| `CompressedLeafV1` | `interface CompressedLeafV1` | A V1 tree's leaf. |
| `CompressedMetadata` | `interface CompressedMetadata` | Bubblegum V2 leaf metadata (MetadataArgsV2): non-fungible, primary sale not happened, mutable unless `isMutable: false`. |
| `CompressedMetadataV2` | `interface CompressedMetadataV2` | A leaf's full MetadataArgsV2, as it is now (with its creators' verified flags and its collection). |
| `CompressedMetadataUpdate` | `interface CompressedMetadataUpdate` | UpdateArgs: what to change (left out: unchanged). |

## Sysvars

Explained in [Sysvars, hashes, signatures and oracles: Sysvars](language-chain.md#sysvars).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `now` | `function now(): i64` | Current cluster unix timestamp (Clock sysvar). |
| `currentSlot` | `function currentSlot(): u64` | The current slot (Clock sysvar). |
| `currentEpoch` | `function currentEpoch(): u64` | The current epoch (Clock sysvar). |
| `epochStartTimestamp` | `function epochStartTimestamp(): i64` | The Unix time the current epoch started at (Clock.epoch_start_timestamp). |
| `slotsPerEpoch` | `function slotsPerEpoch(): u64` | The number of slots in an epoch after warmup (EpochSchedule sysvar). |
| `epochWarmup` | `function epochWarmup(): boolean` | Whether epochs warm up (EpochSchedule sysvar). |
| `firstNormalEpoch` | `function firstNormalEpoch(): u64` | The first epoch after warmup (EpochSchedule sysvar). |
| `firstNormalSlot` | `function firstNormalSlot(): u64` | The first slot after warmup (EpochSchedule sysvar). |
| `lastRestartSlot` | `function lastRestartSlot(): u64` | The LastRestartSlot sysvar: the last slot the cluster restarted at (0 if never). |
| `epochRewards` | `function epochRewards(): EpochRewards` | The EpochRewards sysvar through the `sol_get_epoch_rewards_sysvar` syscall, Rust's `EpochRewards::get()` (no account needed). |
| `EpochRewards` | `interface EpochRewards` | The EpochRewards sysvar, as `epochRewards()` reads it: read-only; keep it in a local (`const er = epochRewards()`). |
| `minimumBalance` | `function minimumBalance(account: AccountMeta): u64` | Rent-exempt minimum for `account`'s current data length. |
| `SlotHashesSysvar` | `interface SlotHashesSysvar` | The SlotHashes sysvar (`SysvarS1otHashes…`), read as an account: it is too large for the sysvar syscalls (Anchor's `Sysvar<SlotHashes>` cannot load it either). |
| `StakeHistorySysvar` | `interface StakeHistorySysvar` | The StakeHistory sysvar (`SysvarStakeHistory…`), read as an account: the cluster's stake per recent epoch (up to 512, newest first), as the Stake program uses it for warmup and cooldown. |
| `stackHeight` | `function stackHeight(): u64` | How deep in cross-program calls this program runs: 1 when the transaction calls it directly, more when another program invoked it. |

## Hashes, signatures and introspection

Explained in [Sysvars, hashes, signatures and oracles: Hashing](language-chain.md#hashing).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sha256` | `function sha256(...parts: (string \| Pubkey \| Hash \| bigint \| boolean)[]): Hash` | sha256 over the parts concatenated: strings (UTF-8), Pubkeys/Hashes (32 bytes), integers (LE), booleans (1 byte). |
| `keccak256` | `function keccak256(...parts: (string \| Pubkey \| Hash \| bigint \| boolean)[]): Hash` | keccak256 over the parts concatenated, encoded as for sha256. |
| `merkleVerify` | `function merkleVerify(leaf: Hash, proof: Vec<Hash>, root: Hash): boolean` | Whether `proof` places `leaf` under `root` (keccak256, sorted pairs: the OpenZeppelin convention most airdrop tools use). |
| `verifyEd25519` | `function verifyEd25519(instructions: InstructionsSysvar, signer: Pubkey, message: string \| Hash \| Pubkey): boolean` | Whether this transaction contains an Ed25519 precompile instruction that verified `message` signed by `signer` (offsets inside the precompile's own data). |
| `verifySecp256k1` | `function verifySecp256k1(hash: Hash, recoveryId: u8, r: Hash, s: Hash, ethAddress: Hash): boolean` | Whether the secp256k1 signer of `hash`, recovered from (r, s, recoveryId), is an Ethereum address given left-padded to 32 bytes (12 zero bytes + 20 address bytes). |
| `ethMessageHash` | `function ethMessageHash(message: string): Hash` | The hash an Ethereum wallet signs for `personal_sign` (EIP-191): keccak256("\x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n" + length + message). |
| `InstructionsSysvar` | `interface InstructionsSysvar` | The Instructions sysvar (Sysvar1nstructions…): every instruction of the transaction being executed. |
| `TransactionInstruction` | `interface TransactionInstruction` | One instruction of the transaction, read from the Instructions sysvar. |

## Oracles and randomness

Explained in [Sysvars, hashes, signatures and oracles: Oracles](language-chain.md#oracles).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PythPriceUpdate` | `interface PythPriceUpdate` | A Pyth `PriceUpdateV2` account (Pyth Solana Receiver, rec5EKMG…). |
| `pythPrice` | `function pythPrice(update: PythPriceUpdate, feedId: Hash, maxAgeSeconds: u64, exponent?: i32): i64` | Like Pyth's get_price_no_older_than: fully verified, `feedId` matches, published within `maxAgeSeconds` (5111 otherwise). |
| `SwitchboardFeed` | `interface SwitchboardFeed<Cluster>` | A Switchboard On-Demand pull feed (PullFeedAccountData). |
| `switchboardValue` | `function switchboardValue(feed: SwitchboardFeed<"mainnet" \| "devnet">, expectedFeed: Pubkey, maxStaleSlots: u64, decimals: u8, minSamples?: u8): i64` | The feed's current result scaled to `decimals` (from 18), if `feed` is `expectedFeed` (anyone can create feeds), it has samples and it is at most `maxStaleSlots` old. |
| `SwitchboardRandomness` | `interface SwitchboardRandomness<Cluster>` | A Switchboard On-Demand randomness account (RandomnessAccountData): verifiable randomness by commit and reveal. |

## Native programs

Explained in [Porting a native program (advanced)](language-native.md).

| Name | Declaration | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `instructionData` | `function instructionData(): InstructionBytes` | The instruction data as sent, discriminator included: `const data = instructionData()`, then `data.length`, `data.get(i)`, or pass it on to `invokeInstruction`. |
| `InstructionBytes` | `interface InstructionBytes` | The instruction data, read in place: its bytes, and little-endian values at a byte offset. |
| `loadRaw` | `function loadRaw<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo): Account<T>` | A native (non-Anchor) program's own account as a fixed-layout struct, as a `#[repr(C)]` type's `load_checked` / `load_mut_checked` reads it: owned by this program (3007) and at least as large as the struct (3003). |
| `loadRawMut` | `function loadRawMut<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo): Mut<T>` | `loadRaw` for writing: also writable and loaded mutably once per instruction (2040). |
| `loadBorsh` | `function loadBorsh<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo): T` | A native program's Borsh account, as Rust's `try_from_slice_unchecked::<T>(&data)` reads it: the data from byte 0 decoded into a local `T` (a copy; write it back with `storeBorsh`). |
| `storeBorsh` | `function storeBorsh<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| Mut<AccountInfo>, value: T): void` | Write `value` into the account's data from byte 0 as Borsh, as Rust's `value.serialize(&mut *data)` does: only the encoded bytes are written (an Option that became None leaves the old bytes after it as they were); an account too small for the encoding fails with `ProgramError.BorshIoError`. |
| `BigVec` | `interface BigVec<T>` | A native program's zero-copy list over the rest of an account (SPL's `big_vec::BigVec`, the stake pool's validator list): a u32 length, then the elements back to back, in an account allocated up front. |
| `BigVecSlice` | `interface BigVecSlice<T>` | Some elements of a BigVec, in place: `bigVec.slice(start, end)`. |
| `loadRawAt` | `function loadRawAt<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64): Account<T>` | `loadRaw` / `loadRawMut` at a byte offset known only at run time (a native account whose parts start where its header says: Phoenix's market at byte 576). |
| `loadRawMutAt` | `function loadRawMutAt<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64): Mut<T>` | `loadRawAt` for writing: writable and claimed as `loadRawMut` is. |
| `rawArrayAt` | `function rawArrayAt<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64, capacity: u64): ReadonlyRawArray<T>` | A read-only view of `capacity` elements of `T` at `offset` in an account (see RawArray); `rawArrayMutAt` writes. |
| `rawArrayMutAt` | `function rawArrayMutAt<T>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64, capacity: u64): RawArray<T>` | `rawArrayAt` for writing: elements set in place (see RawArray). |
| `RawArray` | `interface RawArray<T>` | `capacity` elements of a fixed-size type packed in place from a run-time byte offset, the count known only at run time (a slab sized by its header). |
| `ReadonlyRawArray` | `interface ReadonlyRawArray<T>` | A RawArray of a read-only view (`rawArrayAt`): elements are read, not written. |
| `rbTreeAt` | `function rbTreeAt<K, V>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64, capacity: u64, compare?: (a: K, b: K) => bigint): ReadonlyRedBlackTree<K, V>` | lib-sokoban 0.3's RedBlackTree<K, V, capacity> at a run-time byte offset (see RedBlackTree): owned by this program (3007), its 32 + capacity × (16 + size(K) + size(V)) bytes within the data (ProgramError::AccountDataTooSmall), `rbTreeMutAt` writable and claimed as `loadRawMut` is. |
| `rbTreeMutAt` | `function rbTreeMutAt<K, V>(account: RemainingAccount \| AccountInfo, offset: u64, capacity: u64, compare?: (a: K, b: K) => bigint): RedBlackTree<K, V>` | `rbTreeAt` for writing: insert, remove and initialize with lib-sokoban's own writes (see RedBlackTree). |
| `RedBlackTree` | `interface RedBlackTree<K, V>` | lib-sokoban 0.3's `RedBlackTree<K, V, N>` in account data, byte for byte (Phoenix's order books and trader seats): at the offset, root u32, padding, the allocator (size u64, bump index u32, free list head u32), then `capacity` nodes of 16 register bytes + K + V, 1-based. |
| `ReadonlyRedBlackTree` | `interface ReadonlyRedBlackTree<K, V>` | A RedBlackTree of a read-only view (`rbTreeAt`): read, never changed. |
| `RbEntry` | `interface RbEntry<K, V>` | A node of a RedBlackTree: its key (read-only), its value (in place) and its index in the tree's node array (1-based). |
| `closeRaw` | `function closeRaw(account: RemainingAccount \| Mut<AccountInfo>, receiver: RemainingAccount \| Mut<AccountInfo>): void` | Close an account of this program as a native program does it by hand (Phoenix's Tombstone), in this order: `receiver.lamports += account.lamports`, `account.lamports = 0`, the owner set to the System Program, the data length set to 0 (`realloc(0, false)`: the bytes are not zeroed, the runtime drops them with the length). |
| `assignOwner` | `function assignOwner(account: RemainingAccount \| Mut<AccountInfo>, owner: Pubkey): void` | Set an account's owner in place (Rust's `AccountInfo::assign`). |
| `setReturnData` | `function setReturnData(bytes: IndexedList<u8>): void` | Set this instruction's return data to `bytes` as they are (Rust's `set_return_data(&bytes)`): a list of u8 such as a local `FixedVec<u8, N>`, a Vec or FixedVec in account data, or the instruction data or a slice of it. |
| `panic` | `function panic(message?: string \| null, location?: string): never` | Stop the program as a Rust `panic!` / `unwrap()` on `None` / `unreachable!()` does: the message is logged and the instruction fails with ProgramFailedToComplete (no error code). |
| `panicsAt` | `function panicsAt<T>(location: string, value: T): T` | `value`, with its checked arithmetic panicking as Rust's overflow checks do at `location` ("file:line:column", where the original's expression is): `panicsAt("src/quantities.rs:233:1", a + b)` logs "attempt to add with overflow" there (also "attempt to subtract / multiply with overflow", "attempt to divide by zero", "attempt to calculate the remainder with a divisor of zero", "attempt to negate with overflow", "attempt to divide with overflow", "attempt to shift left / right with overflow" for a shift amount past the width), as `panic` logs (see `PANIC_STYLE`), instead of failing with 5100 / 5101. |
| `abort` | `function abort(): never` | Stop the program as Rust's `abort` does on SBF (the allocator's out-of-memory error, `std::process::abort`): the runtime's `abort` syscall, which fails the instruction with ProgramFailedToComplete and logs "SBF program panicked" (no location, nothing else). |
| `logBase64` | `function logBase64(prefix: string, value: object): void` | Log `prefix` followed by the base64 (standard, padded) of a struct value's bytes, as a native program's `msg!("ray_log: {}", base64(bincode(log)))` does. |
| `logComputeUnits` | `function logComputeUnits(): void` | Log the compute units left (Rust's `sol_log_compute_units()`): the runtime writes "Program consumption: <N> units remaining", as the original's line, at the same place. |

**Next:** [Glossary](glossary.md): the Solana and TypeSOL terms the guide uses.

<!-- docs/glossary.md -->

# Glossary

The Solana and TypeSOL terms the [language guide](language.md) uses, one paragraph each, with the page that uses them
most. Solana's own documentation covers the chain in depth: [solana.com/docs/core](https://solana.com/docs/core).

## Account

A record on the chain at a 32-byte address: a balance in lamports, bytes of data, an owner program and an executable
flag. Programs keep all their state in accounts. See [accounts](language-accounts.md).

## Owner

The word has three meanings in the guide:

- **An account's owner** is the program it belongs to. Only the owner can change the account's data or take lamports
  from it; any program can add lamports to an account the transaction made writable. A new account belongs to the
  System Program until it is assigned to another. See
  [accounts](language-accounts.md#account-parameters-and-the-checks-they-emit).
- **A token account's `owner` field** is the wallet or PDA allowed to move its tokens (its authority), while the
  account itself belongs to the token program. See [tokens](language-cpi.md#tokens).
- **An `owner` field of your own structs** is whatever the program makes of it, usually the key allowed to act on the
  account, checked with `HasOne<…, "owner">` or `require`. See [constraints](language-accounts.md#constraints).

## Lamports

The unit of SOL: 1 SOL is 1,000,000,000 lamports. `account.lamports` is an account's balance, a `u64`.

## Rent

An account must hold a minimum balance proportional to its size to stay on chain, the rent-exempt minimum:
(128 + data bytes) × 6,960 lamports at the time of writing. `create` funds it from the payer, `rentExempt(space)`
computes it, and closing the account returns it. See [creating accounts](language-accounts.md#creating-accounts).

## Discriminator

The first 8 bytes of an account of a TypeSOL or Anchor program (sha256("account:<Name>")[..8]), which say which struct
it holds, and of an instruction's data (sha256("global:<name>")[..8]), which say which instruction it calls. See
[account data](language-basics.md#account-data) and [instructions](language-basics.md#instructions).

## Keypair account

An account whose address is the public key of a keypair made for it, as opposed to a [PDA](#pda): the keypair signs
the transaction that creates it, and afterwards nobody needs it. `create(payer, null)` makes one. See [creating
accounts](language-accounts.md#creating-accounts).

## PDA

A program derived address: an address derived from seeds and a program id that has no private key, so only that
program can sign for it, in its calls to other programs. Programs keep accounts at PDAs so that their addresses can be
derived again. See [PDAs](language-pdas.md).

## Seeds

The byte strings a PDA is derived from (`["vault", owner.key]`): at most 15 of them, plus the bump, each at most 32
bytes. See [seeds](language-pdas.md#seeds).

## Bump

The one byte added to a PDA's seeds so that the derived address has no private key. The canonical bump is the
highest that works; it is found by trying 255, 254, … and is usually stored in the account. See [PDAs](language-pdas.md).

## Signer

An account whose private key signed the transaction (a wallet), or a PDA of the calling program in a call it signs
for. A `Signer` parameter checks it. See [accounts](language-accounts.md#account-parameters-and-the-checks-they-emit).

## Authority

An account allowed to do something to another: a mint's mint authority, a token account's owner, a program's
[upgrade authority](#programdata-and-upgrade-authority), a program's own admin key. It acts by signing, as a wallet or
as a PDA with signer seeds. See [tokens](language-cpi.md#tokens).

## Payer

The account that pays: the fee payer, the transaction's first signer, pays its fees; the payer an instruction names
(`create(payer, …)`) pays the rent of the accounts it creates, so it must sign and be writable (`Mut<Signer>`). See
[creating accounts](language-accounts.md#creating-accounts).

## Writable

Marked writable by the transaction, so its data or lamports may change. A `Mut<…>` parameter checks it.

## Instruction

A call to one program: the program id, the accounts it reads or writes and its data. A TypeSOL instruction is an
exported function. See [instructions](language-basics.md#instructions).

## Transaction

One or more instructions sent together with their signatures, at most 1,232 bytes at the time of writing. It is
atomic: when any instruction fails, the whole transaction fails, its changes are discarded and the fee is still paid.

## Remaining accounts

The accounts a client passes after those an instruction declares, read by position with `remainingAccounts()`
(Anchor's `ctx.remaining_accounts`), for lists whose length is known only at run time. See [remaining
accounts](language-accounts.md#remaining-accounts).

## Return data

Up to 1,024 bytes an instruction leaves for its caller: another program reads them after the call, and a client from
the transaction's simulation or metadata. A TypeSOL instruction that returns a value sends it this way. See [return
values](language-errors-events.md#return-values).

## Program id

A program's address. `programId()` gives it in the program; `typesol.json` records it for each program of a project.

## ProgramData and upgrade authority

An upgradeable program (the BPF upgradeable loader's, which `solana program deploy` uses) is two accounts: the program
account at the program id, which points to a ProgramData account derived from it, and that ProgramData account, which
holds the code, the slot of the last deploy and the upgrade authority. The upgrade authority is the key that may
replace the code; `solana program set-upgrade-authority … --final` removes it, and the program can then never change.
`typesol verify` prints it, and a `ProgramData` parameter reads it, to let only the deployer set a program up. See
[ProgramData](language-accounts.md#programdata) and [deploy to mainnet](mainnet.md).

## System Program

The built-in program that creates accounts, assigns them to an owner and moves lamports out of the accounts it owns
(wallets). See [the System Program](language-cpi.md#the-system-program).

## CPI

A cross-program invocation: one program calling another during an instruction, passing it accounts and, for PDAs,
signer seeds. See [calling other programs](language-cpi.md).

## Slot and epoch

A slot is the time a validator has to produce a block, about 400 ms; an epoch is a run of slots (432,000 on mainnet,
about two days) after which stake activates or deactivates and rewards are paid. `currentSlot()` and `currentEpoch()`
read them from the Clock. See [sysvars](language-chain.md#sysvars).

## Cluster

A network of validators running one Solana chain: mainnet-beta (real SOL), devnet (free SOL for testing), testnet, or a
local validator on your machine (`solana-test-validator`, often called localnet). Commands that send transactions take
the cluster's RPC URL (`--url`). See [deploy to mainnet](mainnet.md).

## Sysvar

An account at a fixed address that holds cluster state: the clock, rent, the epoch schedule and others. See
[sysvars](language-chain.md#sysvars).

## Syscall

A function the runtime provides to programs: logging, hashing, signature recovery, reading sysvars, deriving PDAs,
calling other programs. A program calls it as a function; its cost is in compute units. See
[sysvars](language-chain.md#sysvars).

## Precompile

A native program that verifies signatures (Ed25519, secp256k1, secp256r1) given in an instruction of its own. The
runtime runs it before the transaction's programs and rejects the transaction if a signature is wrong, so a program
only needs to find that instruction in the transaction, through the Instructions sysvar. See
[signatures](language-chain.md#signatures).

## Mint and token account

An SPL Token mint describes a token (its supply, decimals and mint authority); a token account holds an amount of one
mint for an owner, its authority. Both belong to the SPL Token or Token-2022 program. See
[tokens](language-cpi.md#tokens).

## Associated token account

The token account at the address the Associated Token Account program derives from a wallet, the token program and a
mint: the one token account per wallet and mint that wallets and clients use by default. `Ata<…>` checks or creates
one. See [token accounts and mints as
parameters](language-cpi.md#token-accounts-and-mints-as-parameters).

## Borsh

The binary encoding Anchor uses for instruction arguments, events and its account data: integers little-endian,
strings and vectors with a u32 length first. See [types](language-types.md).

## Zero-copy

An account read in place, its bytes used as the struct, instead of being decoded into a copy (Anchor's
`#[account(zero_copy)]` and `AccountLoader`, with bytemuck). TypeSOL reads every fixed-layout account in place;
`@serialization bytemuck` makes the IDL describe a struct as zero-copy, and such an account is checked as Anchor's
`AccountLoader` checks it. See [zero-copy types](language-accounts.md#zero-copy-types-as-anchors-idl-describes-them).

## Anchor

The most used Rust framework for Solana programs: its macros generate each instruction's account checks
(`#[derive(Accounts)]`), account discriminators, error codes and an IDL. TypeSOL follows its conventions (the same
discriminators, error numbers and IDL format), so Anchor clients and tools work with TypeSOL programs, and the guide
names the Anchor equivalent of each feature for readers who know it. Knowing Anchor is not needed. See [migrate from
Anchor](migrate-from-anchor.md).

## IDL

A JSON description of a program's instructions, accounts, types, events and errors, from which clients encode calls
and decode accounts. A TypeSOL build writes one in Anchor's format. See [what the compiler
derives](language-basics.md#what-the-compiler-derives).

## SBF

Solana's bytecode, which programs are compiled to. TypeSOL lowers a program to C and builds it with the platform-tools'
clang.

## Compute units

What an instruction's work is measured in. A transaction gets 200,000 per instruction by default and at most 1,400,000
at the time of writing; past its budget it fails. `typesol profile` shows where a program spends them. See [limits and
costs](language-basics.md#limits-and-costs).

## Next

[The language guide](language.md).

<!-- docs/errors.md -->

# Error codes

Framework errors use Anchor's numbers where Anchor has the same check, so clients and explorers read them the same way.

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 100 / 101 / 102 | instruction data missing / unknown instruction / malformed arguments (InstructionMissing / FallbackNotFound / DidNotDeserialize) |
| 2000 | a `Mut<…>` / `Init<…>` account passed read-only (ConstraintMut) |
| 2001 | HasOne constraint failed (ConstraintHasOne) |
| 2002 | a `Signed<…>` account (or the event authority) did not sign (ConstraintSigner) |
| 2003 | a `constraint(acct, condition)` without its own error failed (ConstraintRaw) |
| 2004 | Owner constraint failed (ConstraintOwner) |
| 2005 | Zeroed account is not rent-exempt (ConstraintRentExempt) |
| 2006 | PDA seeds mismatch (ConstraintSeeds) |
| 2007 | Executable constraint failed (ConstraintExecutable) |
| 2009 | not the associated token account (ConstraintAssociated) |
| 2012 | not the expected address (ConstraintAddress) |
| 2013 | a `Zeroed<…>` account whose discriminator is already set (ConstraintZero; checked before its owner, as under Anchor) |
| 2014 / 2015 | token account mint / owner mismatch (ConstraintTokenMint / ConstraintTokenOwner) |
| 2016 / 2017 / 2018 | mint authority / freeze authority / decimals mismatch (2018: an existing mint `createIfNeeded` found) |
| 2021 / 2022 | token account / mint not owned by the token program `TokenOf` / `MintOf` names (ConstraintTokenTokenProgram / ConstraintMintTokenProgram) |
| 2024–2039 | an existing mint `createIfNeeded` found lacks a Token-2022 extension it was given, or holds other keys in it: group pointer 2024–2026, group member pointer 2027–2029, metadata pointer 2030–2032, close authority 2033–2034, permanent delegate 2035–2036, transfer hook 2037–2039 (the first code of each: the extension is missing; the next: the authority / address differs) (ConstraintMint…Extension…) |
| 2040 | the same account passed in two writable slots (ConstraintDuplicateMutableAccount); also `close(a, b)` in a helper given one account for both |
| 0 (from the System Program) | an `Init` / `create` on an address already in use (AccountAlreadyInUse): the System Program refuses it, as under Anchor's `init` |
| 3000 | `initAccount<T>` on an account whose discriminator is already set (AccountDiscriminatorAlreadySet) |
| 3001 | a zero-copy (`@serialization bytemuck`) account with fewer than 8 bytes of data (AccountDiscriminatorNotFound) |
| 3002 | discriminator mismatch (AccountDiscriminatorMismatch) |
| 3003 | data too small, not an initialized token account / mint, a read past the end, or a `@layout borsh` account whose bytes are not a valid Borsh value (AccountDidNotDeserialize) |
| 3004 | a `@layout borsh` account too small for the value it would now hold (AccountDidNotSerialize) |
| 3005 | not enough accounts (AccountNotEnoughKeys) |
| 3006 | a remaining account or CPI account the program needs writable was passed read-only (AccountNotMutable) |
| 3007 | wrong owner program (AccountOwnedByWrongProgram) |
| 3008 / 3009 | wrong program address / not executable (InvalidProgramId / InvalidProgramExecutable) |
| 3010 | account must sign (AccountNotSigner; also a new keypair account a `create(payer, null, …)` makes) |
| 3011 | a `SystemAccount` owned by another program (AccountNotSystemOwned) |
| 3012 | account not initialized: empty system account where a program account, a token account or a mint was expected (AccountNotInitialized; not for zero-copy accounts, which Anchor's AccountLoader reports as 3007) |
| 3016 | account would grow more than 10 KiB in one instruction (counted from its length when the instruction started), or grow without a payer (AccountReallocExceedsLimit) |
| 4101 | an `Init` / `create` whose payer is the account being created (TryingToInitPayerAsProgramAccount) |
| 4102 | cast overflow (InvalidNumericConversion) |
| 5100 / 5101 | arithmetic overflow (including shifts) / division by zero |
| 5103 | sysvar unavailable |
| 5104 | index out of bounds (arrays, Vecs, remaining accounts, `pop()` on an empty Vec, `push` on a full FixedVec or `pushAll` past its room, a `slice` of the instruction data out of range, a stored `map` / `filter` result one element too small) |
| 5105 | string longer than the FixedString capacity |
| 5106 | missing or mismatched return data |
| 5107 | event larger than 1024 bytes |
| 5108 | empty Option used as a value |
| 5110 | out of heap building strings |
| 5111 | oracle check failed (unverified, stale, wrong feed, no samples) |
| 5112 | data enum is not the variant the code expected |
| 5113 | more accounts in one instruction (or one CPI) than the program takes: 32, or its `MAX_ACCOUNTS` |
| 5114 | a function with a result ended without returning one |
| 5115 | an optional account that was left out was used |
| 6000+ | your error enums' members, in declaration order (imported files first), then one `RequireFailed<N>` error (code 6000 + N, after the highest code) per distinct `require(cond, "message")` string |

A token account or mint parameter fails with 3012 for an empty system account (never created, or closed), 3007 for an account of another program, 3003 for a token program's account that is not an initialized token account (or mint) of its length.

A member's string is its message (the IDL's `msg`); `X = ""` leaves the message out, as an Anchor variant without
`#[msg]`. `/** @code 6200 */` before a member gives it that code, and the members after it continue from there (Anchor's
`Variant = 200`); codes only go up. The tag goes on its own line above the member. `require(cond, "message")` errors come after the highest code.

Any of Anchor's own codes can be raised directly: `require(cond, AnchorError.RequireKeysEqViolated)` fails with 2502,
as `require_keys_eq!` does.

A code can also be computed at run time: `require(cond, code)` with a `u32` value fails with that code. This is how a
helper passes an error on as Rust's `?` does, when it returns the error as a value instead of failing (a price read
whose error the caller may record or ignore): `const r = price(feed); require(r.err === 0n, r.err);`. The code is
reported as it is (use one of your errors' codes, so clients can decode it); a zero code fails with 5100.

## Which error a transaction gets

A transaction can break several checks; it fails with the first. Within each account's constraints the checks run in
the order Anchor's generated code runs them, so a transaction that breaks one check gets the same code under both, and
one that breaks several gets it too except in the cases listed after the steps:

1. The account count (3005), then each account in parameter order: its type, signer (3010), `Mut` (2000); for a
   program account, initialized (3012 for an empty system account), owner (3007), size (3003, the discriminator's 8
   bytes included), then discriminator (3002); a zero-copy one as Anchor's AccountLoader: 3007 / 3001 / 3002, then
   3003; a token account or mint; a program address.
2. Two writable parameters naming one account (2040).
3. The instruction's arguments (102).
4. Each account in parameter order, its constraints in Anchor's order: seeds (2006), associated token account (owner
   2015, then address 2009), `has_one` (2001), `constraint(…)` (2003 or its error), owner (2004), executable (2007), address (2012), then `TokenOf` /
   `MintOf` (2015, 2014, 2021 / 2016, 2017, 2022).

Where TypeSOL's order differs, only a transaction that breaks two of these checks at once sees it:

- Anchor decodes the arguments first, and checks `mut` with the constraints (after seeds and the associated token
  account). TypeSOL decodes the arguments later, after every account's type (step 3), and checks `mut` earlier, with
  the account's type (step 1), which keeps binaries smaller. An instruction with an [account
  group](language-accounts.md#account-groups) decodes its arguments first, as Anchor does, then checks each account in
  order, a group's constraints right after the group's accounts and the other constraints last.
- Too few accounts fails with 3005 before any account is checked; Anchor fails on the first account it cannot find.
- A program account's size is checked before its discriminator; Anchor's `Account::try_from` reads the discriminator
  first (3001 when there are fewer than 8 bytes, 3002 when it differs) and then decodes the data (3003). So an account
  of this program with another discriminator and fewer bytes than the struct fails with 3003 here and 3002 under
  Anchor, and one with fewer than 8 bytes of data with 3003 here and 3001 under Anchor.
- Accounts created by the statements a body starts with (`acct.create(…)`, `createIfNeeded(…)`, `createPda(…)`,
  after its `constraint(…)` lines) are created after steps 1 to 3 and before the constraints of step 4, as Anchor
  creates `init` accounts before checking the other accounts' constraints ([creating
  accounts](language-accounts.md#creating-accounts)). A create written after other statements runs where it is, after
  every check, and so do all creates in an instruction with an account group.
- TypeSOL refuses any two writable parameters naming one account (2040) unless one is `Dup<…>`, where Anchor only compares program and token
  accounts: a signer passed as two writable parameters fails with 2040 here and later, or not at all, under Anchor.

<!-- docs/test-your-program.md -->

# Test your program

`typesol/testing` runs your program in LiteSVM, an in-process Solana runtime: no validator, no SOL, a few
milliseconds per transaction. Projects from `typesol init` already use it in `tests/<name>.test.ts`.

```ts
import { testProgram, type TestProgram } from "typesol/testing";
import { beforeAll, expect, it } from "vitest";

let t: TestProgram;
beforeAll(async () => {
  t = await testProgram("counter", import.meta.url); // builds the program of typesol.json and loads it
});

it("counts", async () => {
  const alice = await t.wallet(); // a funded keypair (10 SOL)
  const counter = await t.pda("counter", alice); // seeds: text, addresses or keypairs, bytes, bigints (u64)
  t.ok(await t.send(alice, t.ix("initialize", {}, { authority: alice, counter })));
  t.ok(await t.send(alice, t.ix("increment", { by: 5n }, { authority: alice, counter })));
  expect((await t.account<{ count: bigint }>("Counter", counter))?.count).toBe(5n);
});
```

## Instructions

`t.pda(...seeds)` derives this program's PDA for the seeds; `t.pdaWithBump(...seeds)` gives `[address, bump]`, for an
instruction that takes the bump as an argument (prefer a stored bump:
[PDAs](language-pdas.md#checking-a-pda-in-the-body)).

`t.ix(name, args, accounts, remaining?)` builds one instruction.

- **Accounts by name**, in camelCase or snake_case. Their signer and writable flags come from the IDL, and accounts
  with a fixed address (the System Program, token programs, sysvars) are filled in, as are PDAs whose seeds are
  constants, arguments or other accounts' keys (`t.ix("initialize", {}, { authority: alice })` derives `counter`). Pass a keypair for an account that
  signs, an address otherwise, and `null` to leave an optional account out.
- **Arguments as plain values:** bigints or numbers for integers, address strings for Pubkeys, `null` for an empty
  Option, objects for structs (camelCase or snake_case fields), arrays for Vecs.
- **Remaining accounts:** `[{ address, writable?, signer? }]`, where `signer` is the account's `KeyPairSigner` (it then
  signs as a signer account; `writable` defaults to false).

`t.send(payer, ...ixs)` sends them in one transaction; keypairs given as accounts sign too.

### Seeds of other widths

`t.pda` takes text, addresses or keypairs, raw bytes, and bigints, which it encodes as 8-byte little-endian u64s, as
the program encodes a `u64` seed. A seed of another width is passed as its bytes: for a program that derives
`["vault", owner.key, index]` with `index: u16`,

```ts
const u16 = (n: number) => {
  const b = new Uint8Array(2);
  new DataView(b.buffer).setUint16(0, n, true); // little-endian, as the program reads a u16 seed
  return b;
};
const vault = await t.pda("vault", alice, u16(3));
t.ok(await t.send(alice, t.ix("open", { index: 3 }, { owner: alice, vault })));
```

`t.pda("vault", alice, 3n)` would be another address (8 bytes for the index). `setUint32` gives a `u32` seed the same
way. A string that is a valid address is taken as an address; pass `new TextEncoder().encode(s)` for text that only
looks like one.

## Results

| Helper | Gives |
| --- | --- |
| `t.ok(res)` | the successful result, or throws with the error, its name (`NotAdmin`) and the program's logs |
| `t.errorCode(res)` | the custom error code of a failed transaction: 6000 + the member's index in your error enum, or a framework code ([errors.md](errors.md)) |
| `t.account(type, address)` | the account decoded by its IDL type (bigints, address strings), or `null` once closed. TypeSOL fixed layouts come back as their IDL structs: a `FixedString<N>` as `{ len, bytes }`, a `FixedVec<T, N>` as `{ len, items }` (the generated client gives strings and arrays) |
| `t.returned(instruction, res)` | the instruction's return data: an integer, boolean, Pubkey or struct |
| `t.balance(address)` | lamports |
| `t.errorName(code)` | the name of an error code: your program's, TypeSOL's or Anchor's |
| `t.connection` | `{ rpc, rpcSubscriptions }` answered by this LiteSVM, for the generated client: `counter.sendInstructions(t.connection, alice, [ix])`, `counter.accounts.Counter.fetch(t.connection.rpc, address)`, views, `resolve`, `watch` and `watchEvents` (as on a cluster: `watch` yields when a later transaction changes the account, not at once; `watchEvents` gets transactions sent after it subscribed, failed ones included in the stream and skipped by the client) |

### Expecting an error

A test that a check holds sends the transaction that breaks it and compares the code. The program here is the vault
of [seeds of other widths](#seeds-of-other-widths), whose `spend` requires `amount <= 10n` and whose only error enum is
`export enum VaultError { TooMuch = "Amount above the limit" }`, so `TooMuch` is 6000 (in the guide's
[`spend`](language-accounts.md#constraints), `NotOwner` comes first and `TooMuch` is 6001):

```ts
const res = await t.send(alice, t.ix("spend", { amount: 50n }, { owner: alice, vault }));
expect(t.errorCode(res)).toBe(6000);
expect(t.errorName(t.errorCode(res))).toBe("TooMuch");
```

`t.errorCode` throws when the transaction succeeded or failed without a custom code (a runtime error such as missing
signatures), so the test fails then too.

## Tokens and time

| Helper | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `t.mint({ authority, decimals?, supply?, freezeAuthority?, tokenProgram?, address? })` | writes a mint straight into the VM, as CreateAccount + InitializeMint2 leave it (SPL Token unless `tokenProgram` is Token-2022; no extensions), and returns its address |
| `t.tokenAccount({ mint, owner, amount?, tokenProgram?, address? })` | writes a token account holding `amount`; pass `address` for an associated token account |
| `t.tokenBalance(address)` | the amount a token account holds, or `null` when it does not exist |
| `t.warp({ unixTimestamp?, slot?, seconds? })` | moves the Clock: to a timestamp or slot, or forward by `seconds` |

## Accounts from a cluster

To test against accounts that exist on mainnet (a mint, an oracle, another program), list them in `typesol.json` as
`"clone": ["<address>", …]` and run `typesol clone --url mainnet-beta` once (or `typesol clone <address>…`). They are
written to `tests/accounts/`, which `testProgram` loads into its LiteSVM before your first test; commit the directory so
the tests run offline. `loadClonedAccounts(svm, dir)` does the same for a LiteSVM of your own.

`t.svm`, `t.programId`, `t.idl` and `t.coder` are there for anything else. `programHarness(svm, programId, idl)` gives the same helpers for a
program you loaded yourself, and `svmConnection(svm)` the RPC pair alone (for any LiteSVM, e.g. one with an Anchor
program loaded). Transactions sent through it run at once; `getProgramAccounts` (`fetchAll`) sees the accounts those
transactions named, plus any you `track(...)`.

The module needs `litesvm` and `@anchor-lang/core`, which `typesol init` adds to `devDependencies`.

## Epochs and staking

LiteSVM's `warpToSlot` leaves `Clock.epoch` where it was, and its StakeHistory stays empty, so the Stake program takes
every delegation as fully active one epoch after it was made. For a program that stakes, these helpers make epochs and
warmup / cooldown behave as on a cluster:

| Helper | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `warpToEpoch(svm, epoch, { secondsPerSlot? })` | moves the Clock to the first slot of `epoch` by the VM's EpochSchedule (warmup epochs included): slot, epoch, leader schedule epoch, `unixTimestamp` (+0.4 s a slot by default) and `epochStartTimestamp`; expires the blockhash. `nextEpoch(svm)` moves one epoch |
| `new StakeCluster(svms, opts?)` | one or more LiteSVMs that get the same Clock, EpochSchedule and StakeHistory. `cluster.nextEpoch()` / `cluster.warpToEpoch(e)` end each epoch as a cluster does: the StakeHistory gets the epoch's entry (the sum of every stake account's activation at that epoch, plus `base`, the rest of the cluster), then the Clock moves on. `cluster.activation(stake)` gives a stake account's `{ effective, activating, deactivating }` now |
| `stakeActivation(delegation, epoch, history, newRateActivationEpoch?, { math? })` | a delegation's activation at an epoch: an exact port of the Stake program's `stake_activating_and_deactivating_v2` (solana-stake-interface 4.3.0) |
| `createVoteAccount(svm, payer, { node?, voter?, withdrawer?, commission? })` | a vote account made by the Vote program; returns its address |
| `createStakeAccount(svm, payer, { staker, withdrawer, lamports, lockup? })` | a stake account made by the Stake program, `lamports` in all (rent-exempt minimum included) |
| `delegateStake(svm, payer, { stake, vote, staker? })` | delegates it |
| `readStakeAccount(svm, address)` | the account's StakeStateV2: `{ kind: "Stake", meta, stake: { delegation, creditsObserved }, stakeFlags }`, `Initialized`, `Uninitialized` or `RewardsPool`; `null` when it does not exist |
| `readStakeHistory(svm)` / `writeStakeHistory(svms, entries)` | the StakeHistory sysvar as a `Map` of epoch → `stakeHistoryEntry(effective, activating, deactivating)` |

```ts
const cluster = new StakeCluster([original.svm, port.svm], { base: stakeHistoryEntry(1000n * SOL) });
const vote = await createVoteAccount(original.svm, payer);
// ... the program under test delegates a stake account
cluster.nextEpoch(); // 9% of the cluster's effective stake may warm up per epoch: 90 SOL here
expect(cluster.activation(stake).effective).toBe(90n * SOL);
```

- **The rest of the cluster.** `base` defaults to 400M SOL effective with nothing activating or deactivating: as on
  mainnet, a delegation under 36M SOL warms up in one epoch. Give a smaller `effective`, or `activating` /
  `deactivating` above 9% of it, to make warmup and cooldown take several epochs; `base` may also be a function of
  the epoch. With `allStakeAccounts: false` only the accounts passed to `cluster.track(...)` count.
- **One history for every VM.** The delegations are read from the first VM; the Clock and EpochSchedule of the first
  VM are copied to the others when the cluster is made, so a differential test's two VMs see the same sysvars.
- **No gaps.** The Stake program finds an entry by its distance from the newest one, which must be the previous
  epoch's: a history that skips an epoch is misread. The cluster writes one entry per epoch it passes; it refuses a VM
  whose history stops before the previous epoch or has an entry for the current epoch or a later one (an epoch that
  has not ended), and `cluster.warpToEpoch` / `nextEpoch` refuse to go on once the Clock was moved past the history
  some other way. Warping a VM with stake accounts by `warpToEpoch` alone leaves the history behind.
- **A new LiteSVM's slot.** Its Clock is at epoch 0 but at slot 454,464,000; the first warp moves the slot back to the
  first slot of the epoch warped to (32 for epoch 1 by the default warmup schedule), the timestamps forward.
- **Float or integer.** The Stake program in LiteSVM 1.6.1 computes warmup and cooldown with f64 (the algorithm
  solana-stake-interface 4.3.0 keeps as the deprecated `stake_activating_and_deactivating`); Stake program 5.1
  (SIMD-0391) uses basis-point integers. They differ by a few lamports once amounts pass 2^53 lamports (about 9M SOL).
  `StakeCluster` uses `math: "float"` by default, so its history and `activation` match LiteSVM to the lamport;
  `stakeActivation` uses the integer algorithm unless given `{ math: "float" }`. Both take the 9% rate from epoch 0
  (`newRateActivationEpoch` 0, as the Stake program has it); `null` gives the original 25%.
- **Rent.** In LiteSVM 1.6.1 the Stake program holds back the Rent sysvar's minimum for 200 bytes
  (`svm.minimumBalanceForRentExemption(200n)`), which is less than the `rentExemptReserve` its Initialize stores.

<!-- docs/cli.md -->

# CLI reference

`typesol <command> --help` prints the same text for one command. Options are checked: an unknown option is an
error. Exit codes: **0** success, **1** failure (compile errors, failed deploy, …), **2** usage error,
**3** `verify` mismatch.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `typesol init [<dir>] [--name <program>] [--template counter\|vault\|escrow] [--no-agent-files]` | Create a project ([below](#typesol-init)). |
| `typesol new <program> [--template counter\|vault\|escrow]` | In a project: add a program, `programs/<program>.ts` and `tests/<program>.test.ts` from the template, and its entry in `typesol.json`. Refuses to overwrite files or reuse a name. |
| `typesol doctor [--url <rpc>] [--config <cli config>]` | Check what building, testing and deploying need: Node.js, the platform-tools (and a `toolchain` row: the tested ones, or untested with both versions), the Solana CLI, Docker (optional: only `--docker` builds need it; it says when they run emulated), its keypair, the RPC (`--url`, a cluster moniker, or the CLI config) and the keypair's balance there, and the project. Each problem is printed with the command that fixes it. The last line says what is ready (building and testing, or also deploying) and what the warnings concern. Exit code 1 when building is impossible (Node.js or the platform-tools missing); deploy pieces are warnings. |
| `typesol build [<program>…] [--sbpf v0\|v1\|v2] [--profile] [--toolchain-strict] [--docker [--typesol-version <v>] [--release-record <file>]] [--quiet]` | In a project: build every program (or those named) into `<out>/<name>/`: `<name>.so`, `<name>.json` (Anchor IDL), `<name>.client.ts` (TypeScript client, see [client.md](client.md)), `<name>.c`, `<name>.build.json` (the TypeSOL, TypeScript, clang and platform-tools versions, the host, the SBPF version, each source's sha256 and the binary's). With platform-tools other than the tested ones it warns once; `--toolchain-strict` (or `TYPESOL_TOOLCHAIN=strict`) refuses them. The first build creates `<out>/deploy/<name>-keypair.json` and records the address in `typesol.json`; later builds refuse a different keypair. Without the keypair (a fresh clone, CI) it builds at the recorded address and says so; only `deploy` needs the keypair. `--docker` builds in the pinned container instead ([below](#build---docker-and-verify---docker)). |
| `typesol build <file.ts> [--out <dir>] [--program-id <keypair.json>] [--sbpf …] [--profile] [--toolchain-strict] [--docker …] [--quiet]` | Outside a project (or a file that is not one of its programs): build that file. Its keypair is `--program-id`, which must exist, or `<out>/<name>-keypair.json`, created on the first build. A project program's `.ts` builds as that program. |
| `typesol check [<program>… \| <file.ts>] [--json] [--stdin \| --files]` | Type-check and validate without building. In a project, no argument checks every program (or those named) and exits 1 if any has errors. `--json` prints `{ ok, diagnostics: [{ file, line, column, message }] }`, always (a missing file or unreadable `--files` input is a diagnostic too, exit 1 or 2); `--stdin` checks the text given on stdin as that file (its imports come from disk); `--files` reads `{ "files": { "<absolute path>": "<text>", … } }` from stdin and checks with those texts instead of the disk (an editor's unsaved buffers). |
| `typesol clone [<address>…] [--url <rpc>] [--config <cli config>] [--out <dir>]` | Copy cluster accounts and programs for the tests (Anchor's `[test.validator.clone]`): each account to `<address>.json` (lamports, owner, data), each program to `<address>.so` (its ELF, from the ProgramData account for upgradeable programs), in `tests/accounts` (`"accounts"` in `typesol.json`) or `--out`. Without addresses it clones the project's `"clone"` list. `testProgram` loads that directory into its LiteSVM; commit it so the tests run offline. |
| `typesol emit-c <file.ts> [--out <file.c>] [--profile]` | Print or write the generated C. |
| `typesol mcp` | Serve the Model Context Protocol on stdio for AI coding agents: tools to check a program (errors with hints), read its IDL, search the docs and read the rules a TypeSOL program follows. The `.mcp.json` / `.cursor/mcp.json` that `init` writes start it as `npx --no-install typesol mcp` (the project's own copy); see [ai.md](ai.md). |
| `typesol deploy [<program>…] [--url <rpc>] [--keypair <payer.json>] [--config <cli config>] [--dry-run] [--sbpf …] [--toolchain-strict]` | Build (`--toolchain-strict` as for `build`), then `solana program deploy --use-rpc` at the program keypair's address. Deploying again upgrades (the payer must be the upgrade authority). `--dry-run` builds and prints the commands. It needs a cluster, `--url` or `json_rpc_url` in the Solana CLI config: it never falls back to the CLI's default. Before sending anything it checks that the payer keypair exists (if not, it stops with `solana-keygen new`), prints the cluster's host and the payer, checks that the RPC answers and that the payer holds enough for the rent (about twice the binary's on a first deploy, while the buffer exists), and says what to do if not (start `solana-test-validator`, `solana airdrop` on devnet or a local validator). Needs `solana` on PATH. |
| `typesol idl publish [<program>…] [--url <rpc>] [--keypair <authority.json>] [--config <cli config>] [--non-canonical]` | Compile (the binary is not rebuilt), then write each IDL to the Program Metadata program (seed `idl`). Canonical IDLs must be signed by the upgrade authority. Defaults come from the Solana CLI config (`~/.config/solana/cli/config.yml`); it prints the cluster's host and the payer before sending. |
| `typesol cpi <idl.json> [--out <file.ts>] [--prefix <name>] [--address <base58>]` | Generate TypeSOL helpers that call another program from its IDL. Unsupported instructions are listed on stderr. |
| `typesol port <idl.json> [--out <file.ts>]` | A TypeSOL program skeleton from an Anchor IDL (0.30+/1.x), to port an Anchor program: account structs, enums, errors, events and one function per instruction with its accounts and arguments, each body `require(false, …NotPorted)` until written. Instruction discriminators (an explicit `@discriminator` when the name derives another), account names and error codes are kept, so existing clients keep working where the layouts match; notes on stderr list where they do not (Borsh `String`/`Option` in account data, a `Vec` that is not the last field). Error codes that skip ahead are kept with `@code`, and zero-copy types keep their IDL `repr`, `serialization` and field names (`@repr`, `@serialization`, `@idlName`). |
| `typesol client <idl.json> [--out <file.ts>] [--address <base58>]`, `typesol client --address <program id> [--url <rpc>] [--config <cli config>] [--out <file.ts>]` | Generate a typed TypeScript client on `@solana/kit` from an Anchor IDL (0.30+/1.x or TypeSOL); the IDL is validated first, and what the client leaves out is printed as notes. Without a file, the IDL is read from the chain: the canonical Program Metadata IDL, else Anchor's IDL account. See [client.md](client.md). |
| `typesol verify <program\|file.ts> [<deployed.so>] [--address <program id>] [--url <rpc>] [--config <cli config>] [--sbpf …] [--manifest <name.build.json>] [--docker …]` | Rebuild and compare with what is deployed ([below](#typesol-verify)). |
| `typesol profile <logs.txt\|-> [--program <id>]` | Compute units per TypeScript line from the logs of a `--profile` build's transaction (exit 1 when the logs have no markers). |
| `typesol help <command>` | Same as `typesol <command> --help`. |
| `typesol --version` | Print the version. |

`clone`, `client --address`, `verify` and `idl publish` give up on an RPC request after 30 seconds
(`TYPESOL_RPC_TIMEOUT=<seconds>` changes it) and, like `doctor` and `deploy`, name only the RPC's host and the cause
when one fails (an RPC URL can carry an API key). A `--config` file that does not exist is a usage error everywhere.

Builds (`build`, `deploy`, `verify`, `typesol/testing`) compare the active clang with the one the release is tested
with (`TESTED_TOOLCHAIN` in `typesol/compiler`: Agave 3.1.10, platform-tools v1.52): another one gets one warning per
process on stderr. `TYPESOL_TOOLCHAIN=strict` makes it an error everywhere, `warn` is the default.

## typesol init

`typesol init [<dir>] [--name <program>] [--template counter|vault|escrow] [--no-agent-files]` creates a project:

- `typesol.json`, `programs/<name>.ts`, `tests/<name>.test.ts` (LiteSVM), `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`,
  `programs/tsconfig.json` (with the editor plugin), `.vscode/settings.json` (the workspace TypeScript, so the plugin
  loads) and `.gitignore`;
- the rules for AI coding agents (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` importing it, `.cursor/rules/typesol.mdc`) and the MCP
  server configuration (`.mcp.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`; see [ai.md](ai.md)). `--no-agent-files` leaves them out
  (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/`, `.mcp.json`); otherwise `init` lists them after the files it created.

`<name>` must be snake_case; by default it is derived from `<dir>` (`my-app` → `my_app`). The template picks the
program and its test: `counter` (default, a PDA counter per user), `vault` (SOL at a PDA: deposit, withdraw above
rent, close) or `escrow` (SPL tokens: make, take, refund, the offer PDA signing for its vault). `init` refuses to
overwrite files. It warns, with the install commands, when the platform-tools that building needs are missing, and
says whether the Agave CLI is missing or only its platform-tools (on Linux arm64, where there is no Agave CLI, the
commands that set up the platform-tools' `linux-aarch64` package).

## typesol verify

`typesol verify <program|file.ts> [<deployed.so>] [--address <program id>] [--url <rpc>] [--config <cli config>]
[--sbpf …] [--manifest <name.build.json>] [--docker …]` rebuilds the program and compares it with what is deployed.

- **Without a `.so`** it reads the program from the cluster (`--url`, cluster monikers such as `mainnet-beta` included,
  else the Solana CLI config) at `--address` or the address `typesol.json` records, under any loader (v2, upgradeable
  v3, v4). It prints the upgrade authority (or that the program is immutable) and the last deploy slot, and compares
  the IDL published with `typesol idl publish` (a published IDL that differs is a mismatch).
- **With a `.so`** (e.g. from `solana program dump`) it compares with that file.
- Trailing zero padding is ignored; the SBPF version is read from the deployed ELF unless `--sbpf` is given.
- **On a mismatch** it prints the rebuild's toolchain (clang, platform-tools, host, TypeSOL) and the deployed build's
  when a build manifest's binary hash is the deployed bytes' (`--manifest`, `<deployed>.build.json` next to a given
  `.so`, or the local build's), and what differs; otherwise it says the deployed side's toolchain is unknown (a
  program on chain records none). A host difference alone is named as such; it counts only between builds of 0.44.1
  or earlier, whose programs with 128-bit or signed division linked platform-tools' compiler-builtins (laid out
  differently by each host package).
- `--docker` rebuilds in the pinned container and, on a match, prints what was verified
  ([below](#build---docker-and-verify---docker)).

## build --docker and verify --docker

`--docker` builds in a container made on your machine from `docker/Dockerfile` (shipped in the package): linux/amd64
on every machine (emulated on arm64), Node 24, the platform-tools v1.52 of Agave 3.1.10, and a TypeSOL version from
npm whose tarball is checked against `releases/<version>.json` (sha512 integrity, sha1 shasum, every file's sha256)
before it is installed, with its npm dependencies installed by `npm ci` from `docker/deps/<version>.lock.json` (every
package checked against the lock's integrity; the package's lock, or the version's own tarball's). Every input is
pinned by digest, checksum or integrity. The image is `typesol-build:<version>-<first 12
of the Dockerfile's sha256>`, built the first time it is needed (progress on stderr; about 750 MB of downloads) and
reused after. Builds run with `--network none`, the sources read-only (the project root, or a single file's
directory: imports from outside it are not there), the output directory writable, no capabilities, a read-only root
file system, as your uid and gid (root for a root caller, still without capabilities). The written files are the
ones `build` writes; `<name>.build.json` adds `container` (platform, Dockerfile sha256, base images, downloads, the
TypeSOL tarball's hashes and the commit its record names, where the release record came from and the record's sha256,
the dependency lock with its sha256, the local image id). An image is reused only when its labels carry this
record's integrity, shasum, commit and file list and this lock's sha256; an image of the same tag made from other
values is an error that names it (remove it to build from this record).

| Option | |
| --- | --- |
| `--typesol-version <v>` | The TypeSOL in the container. Default: this `typesol`'s version (in a project that installs another `typesol` than the one running, an error naming both); for `verify`, the version of the deployed build's manifest when one is known (`--manifest`, `<deployed>.build.json`, or the local build's whose binary hash is the deployed one's). |
| `--release-record <file>` | The record to check that version's tarball against. Default: the package's (a package ships the records of the releases before it: a record is written after its release is published), else `releases/<version>.json` fetched from the repository's main branch over HTTPS (said on stderr; where it came from and the sha256 of its bytes go into `container.typesol.record`), so that the npm tarball is checked against a second, independent source (as with a file given here; a record the package ships came from npm too). Offline, or for a version the repository has no record of, an error names this option. Versions before 0.43.0 have no record and are refused. |

Without Docker, with its daemon stopped or when the image build fails, `--docker` is an error and nothing is built;
it never falls back to the local toolchain. `TYPESOL_DOCKER_CPUS` and `TYPESOL_DOCKER_MEMORY` (e.g. `2`, `4g`) limit
the build container on a shared machine. Why one platform: [stability.md](stability.md#what-builds-the-same-bytes-where).

## typesol.json

```json
{
  "programs": { "vault": { "path": "programs/vault.ts", "address": "…recorded on first build…" } },
  "out": "target",
  "sbpf": "v0"
}
```

`"clone": ["<address>", …]` lists the cluster accounts `typesol clone` copies for the tests, and `"accounts"` where
they are kept (default `tests/accounts`). `"programs": { "vault": "programs/vault.ts" }` (a plain path) is accepted too. Keep `target/deploy/*-keypair.json`
safe and out of git: it is the program's address, and it is needed to deploy it again. A clone without
it still builds and tests (`npm test` builds first) at the recorded address; deploying needs it.

## Editor

`typesol init` projects load `typesol/ts-plugin` from `programs/tsconfig.json`: besides TypeScript's errors, the editor
underlines what the TypeSOL compiler refuses (an unsupported construct, a constraint that cannot hold…), for the text
being edited (unsaved changes in every open file), once TypeScript itself has nothing to report. It checks the program
entries listed in `typesol.json` and shows each problem in the file it is in, the entry or any file it imports. The
compiler runs inside the editor's TypeScript server once it has loaded (a check takes milliseconds; the first ones run
`typesol check --json --files` as a child process). Editors load tsconfig plugins from the project's own TypeScript:
`typesol init` writes `.vscode/settings.json` so VS Code offers to switch to it ("Use Workspace Version"). To add the
plugin to an existing project:

```json
{ "compilerOptions": { "plugins": [{ "name": "typesol/ts-plugin" }] } }
```

<!-- docs/client.md -->

# TypeScript client

Every `typesol build` writes a typed client next to the program: `<out>/<name>/<name>.client.ts`. It is one file, it
depends only on [`@solana/kit`](https://github.com/anza-xyz/kit) (8.5 or later), and it is rewritten on every build, so
it always matches the program. `typesol client <idl.json>` writes the same kind of client from an Anchor IDL (Anchor 0.30+
and 1.x), so one client style covers TypeSOL programs and the Anchor programs they talk to. `typesol client --address
<program id> --url <rpc>` reads the IDL from the chain instead: the canonical Program Metadata IDL (`typesol idl
publish`, Codama), else Anchor's IDL account (`anchor idl init`), so any deployed Anchor or TypeSOL program with a
published IDL gets a client from its address alone.

```ts
import { ledgerbook } from "./target/ledgerbook/ledgerbook.client.js";

// Instructions: fixed addresses (System Program, token programs, ...) and PDAs are filled in from the IDL.
const create = await ledgerbook.create({ admin: signer }, { title: "grants", approver: null });

// PDAs
const [book] = await ledgerbook.pdas.book({ admin: signer.address, title: "grants" });
const file = await ledgerbook.file({ who: signer, book }, { amount: 100n, note: "rent", memo: null });

// Accounts: decode bytes you already have, or fetch through an RPC.
const bookData = await ledgerbook.accounts.Book.fetch(rpc, book); // { title: string, approver: Address | null, entries: [...], ... }

// Send and confirm (one transaction, signers in the accounts sign too), or simulate
const signature = await ledgerbook.sendInstructions({ rpc, rpcSubscriptions }, signer, [create, file]);
const { err, logs, unitsConsumed, returnData } = await ledgerbook.simulate(rpc, signer, [file]);

// Errors: by name, from a kit SolanaError, a LiteSVM result, a simulation message or a code.
if (ledgerbook.isError(e, "NotApprover")) { /* ... */ }
ledgerbook.errorCode(e); // 6002

// Events written by `emit`, from a transaction's log messages
for (const ev of ledgerbook.parseEvents(logs)) if (ev.name === "Filed") ev.data.amount;

// Return data of an instruction that returns a value, or the value itself by simulation (Anchor's `.view()`)
ledgerbook.returns.total(returnDataBytes); // bigint
await ledgerbook.views.total(rpc, signer, { book }, { status: Status.Approved }); // bigint, nothing sent

// Every Book of the program, or those with given bytes at an offset (after the 8-byte discriminator)
const books = await ledgerbook.accounts.Book.fetchAll(rpc); // [{ address, data }]
const several = await ledgerbook.accounts.Book.fetchMultiple(rpc, [book, otherBook]); // (Book | null)[]

// Live updates, until the AbortSignal aborts
for await (const book of ledgerbook.accounts.Book.watch(rpcSubscriptions, address, { abortSignal })) render(book);
for await (const { signature, event } of ledgerbook.watchEvents(rpcSubscriptions, { abortSignal, rpc })) show(event); // with rpc: emitCpi events too

// Remaining accounts go after the instruction's own (Anchor's `.remainingAccounts([...])`)
await ledgerbook.approveMany({ approver: signer, book }, { indices: [0n, 1n] }, [{ address: extra, role: AccountRole.WRITABLE }]);

// has_one accounts that do not sign, read from the account that names them (Anchor resolves `relations` the same way)
const accounts = await ledgerbook.resolve.someInstruction(rpc, { book }, { signer }); // signers, and what book's fields name

// Events of a fetched transaction (getTransaction, json): log events and emitCpi events from inner instructions
ledgerbook.eventsOf(await rpc.getTransaction(signature, { encoding: "json", maxSupportedTransactionVersion: 0 }).send());
```

Signer accounts take a `TransactionSigner`, which kit uses to sign; an `Address` works too when you sign separately.
Kit's own transaction functions work with the instructions as well; `sendInstructions` is that pipeline in one call.

## What the client contains

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `<program>.<instruction>(accounts, args)` | Builds the `Instruction`. Accounts with a fixed address and PDAs whose seeds are constants, arguments (an Option one with its default too: Anchor's `id.unwrap_or(0)`) or other accounts' keys are optional and filled in; pass one to override. An optional account passed as `null` is left out (sent as the program id, the convention TypeSOL and Anchor share); left undefined, it is filled in like any other. |
| `<program>.<instruction>(accounts, args, remaining?)` | The same, with remaining accounts appended in order (kit `AccountMeta`s). |
| `<program>.accounts.<Name>` | `decode(bytes)`, `encode(value)`, `fetch(rpc, address)`, `fetchMaybe(rpc, address)`, `fetchMultiple(rpc, addresses)`, `fetchAll(rpc, filters?)` (getProgramAccounts by discriminator, plus `{ offset, bytes }` filters), `watch(rpcSubscriptions, address, { abortSignal })`, `discriminator`. `decode` checks the discriminator. |
| `<program>.pdas.<account>(seeds)` | The PDA (address and bump) for each account an instruction derives, also one seeded from its own fields (from the field values). |
| `<program>.returns.<instruction>(bytes)` | Decodes return data. |
| `<program>.resolve.<instruction>(rpc, accounts, args?, { signer? })` | Fills in what needs the chain or the wallet: signer accounts left out (`options.signer`, the default signer, like Anchor's provider wallet), `has_one` accounts that do not sign (read from the account that names them), and PDAs seeded from another account's fields, scalars, strings or bytes (`seeds = [b"vault", book.owner]`: the account is read, then the PDA derived). Given accounts are kept. |
| `<program>.views.<instruction>(rpc, feePayer, accounts, args)` | Simulates an instruction that returns a value and decodes it (throws with the logs if it fails). |
| `<program>.sendInstructions(connection, feePayer, instructions)`, `simulate(rpc, feePayer, instructions)` | One transaction sent and confirmed (kit's sendAndConfirm), or simulated without signatures (error, logs, units, this program's return data). |
| `<program>.errors`, `errorCode(e)`, `isError(e, name)` | The program's errors (6000+), and for TypeSOL programs also every Anchor framework error (`AnchorError` and the constraints raise them) and TypeSOL's runtime errors. |
| `<program>.parseEvents(logs)`, `parseCpiEvents(data)`, `eventsOf(tx)`, `watchEvents(rpcSubscriptions, { abortSignal })` | Events from `Program data:` log lines, from `emitCpi` inner instructions (bytes or base58), from a fetched transaction (both), or live from log subscriptions. |
| Types and codecs | Every defined type as a TypeScript type (`Book`, the decoded value) and an input type (`BookArgs`, which also accepts `number` for 64- and 128-bit integers), with a kit codec (`getBookCodec()`). |

Types follow the program's TypeScript: `u64`/`i64`/`u128`/`i128` are `bigint` (inputs accept `number` too), smaller
integers and floats are `number`, `Pubkey` is kit's `Address`, `string` and `FixedString<N>` are `string`, `Option<T>` is
`T | null`, unit enums are const objects (`Status.Pending`, also usable as a type), and data enums are unions on `kind`,
as in the program. Names are camelCase. For Anchor IDLs, data enums use `__kind`, as Codama-generated clients do. The
file uses no TypeScript-only syntax (no `enum`), so it also runs under Node's type stripping.

Anchor IDLs can also hold types a TypeSOL program does not: `u256`/`i256` are `bigint` (32 bytes, little-endian), and
`Option<Option<T>>` is `Option<T> | null` with kit's `Option` inside, so the three values stay apart: `null` is None,
`none()` is Some(None) and `some(x)` (or `x`) is Some(Some(x)). A type that holds itself through a Vec or an Option
(`enum Shape { Dot, Rec { kids: Vec<Shape> } }`) is encoded and decoded to any depth.

## Safety

An IDL can come from anywhere, so `typesol client` refuses one whose names are not identifiers, whose discriminators or
seed bytes are not bytes, or whose error codes are not integers, before anything reaches the output. Older (pre-0.30)
Anchor IDLs are refused with a hint to convert them (`anchor idl convert`).

## Limits

- **Errors are matched by code, not by program**: a program this one calls can raise the same error code. Events are
  this program's own: `parseEvents` follows the `Program <id> invoke` / `success` / `failed` lines and reads a
  `Program data:` line only while this program is the innermost one running, and `eventsOf` reads only the `emitCpi`
  inner instructions that call this program (it needs `tx.transaction`'s account keys for that). `parseCpiEvents(data)`
  on its own does not check the program: give it this program's inner instructions only.
- **Not filled in by the builder** (pass them): PDAs seeded from a field of another account's data (`state.owner`;
  `resolve` reads the account and derives them), PDAs whose program is another account's field, and a PDA seeded from
  its own fields (derive it with its `pdas` helper from the values). `typesol client` prints a note for each. PDAs
  seeded from a field of a struct argument, at any depth (`params.inner.id`), are filled in.
- **Left out, with a note**: instructions, accounts and types using `Option<Option<Option<T>>>` or deeper, and types
  the client cannot express (listed by `typesol client`).
- **Anchor IDLs**: zero-copy (`bytemuck`) accounts decode and encode at their `#[repr(C)]` offsets as the program sees
  them on SBF (padding included; `packed` and `align` honored; 128-bit integers align to 8). Generic types become one
  type per use with concrete arguments (`Pair<u64, 2>` is `PairU64N2`). Left out, with a note: zero-copy types with
  Rust's own layout (`repr(Rust)`) or holding a non-zero-copy type, and the generic definitions themselves.
- **In tests**: `svmConnection(svm)` from `typesol/testing` answers the client's RPC calls from LiteSVM, and
  `testProgram(...)` has it as `t.connection` ([test-your-program.md](test-your-program.md)).
- `watchEvents` reads log events of transactions that succeeded (a failed one is skipped); with `rpc` it also fetches each transaction in which the program invoked itself and
  reads its `emitCpi` events (log subscriptions do not carry inner instructions).

<!-- docs/migrate-from-anchor.md -->

# Migrate from Anchor

TypeSOL programs speak Anchor's wire format: the same instruction and account discriminators, Borsh arguments, an
Anchor-format IDL, the same error numbering and event logs. A ported program can keep its clients. This page maps
Anchor's constructs to TypeSOL's and shows the porting workflow. For one complete program ported this way, with the
original side by side, the checks run against it and its cost, see [Case study: porting Anchor's escrow](case-study-escrow.md).

## Start from the IDL

```sh
anchor build                                   # in the Anchor project: target/idl/my_program.json
npx @typesol/cli init my-program && cd my-program
npm install                                    # the project's own TypeSOL, run below as npx --no-install typesol
rm programs/my_program.ts tests/my_program.test.ts   # the counter template's program and test
npx --no-install typesol port ../anchor/target/idl/my_program.json --out programs/my_program.ts
```
